title: The Distributionally Robust Cyclic Inventory Routing Problem
summary: We study the cyclic inventory routing problem that involves joint decisions on vehicle routing and inventory replenishment on an infinite, cyclic horizon. It considers a single warehouse and a set of geographically dispersed retailers. We model retailer demand as random variables with uncertain distributions belonging to a moment-based ambiguity set. We develop a distributionally robust optimization formulation that minimizes the worst-case expected cost over the ambiguity set, while ensuring service reliability through a distributionally robust chance constraint.
